newsitem.title: USA: Wider US Q3 trade gap aberration-Commerce's Kantor.
newsitem.headline: Wider US Q3 trade gap aberration-Commerce's Kantor.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor Friday called the third-quarter widening in the U.S. trade deficit an aberration.

"The third quarter seems to be an aberration," Kantor said during a news conference after the release of data showing the November U.S. trade gap increasing to $8.4 billion -- well below economists' forecasts.
Kantor expressed optimism that the nation's trade deficit will continue to narrow as exports continue to rise.
"I'm very optimistic that we'll continue to moderate the trade deficit," Kantor said.

The outgoing Commerce Secretary said he remained concerned about the U.S. trade gap with China despite a narrowing of that deficit to $3.0 billion in November from $4.9 billion in October. "We're still concerned about our trade with China (but) that's good news," Kantor said.
He noted the deficit with Japan dropped by $642 million in November.

Kantor said an economic recovery in Japan is important to the United States. "We want to make sure we do everything we can to be helpful," he said. "But this is up to the Japanese leadership and the Japanese people."
Kantor said he expects Chile to become a party to the North American Free Trade Agreement.
"I believe Chile is ready to accede ...to NAFTA," he said. "I think it's not a matter of whether Chile accedes to the NAFTA, I think it's when."
He predicted the move would take place "fairly rapidly" after fast-track trade authority is granted by Congress.
Kantor said President Clinton remains committed to securing "fast-track" trade authority in 1997.
